name: Bijagós Archipelago Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Mangroves, seagrass and mudflats where turtles, manatees and migrant waders feed.

tip.title: Thin the seagrass
tip.text: Green turtles and manatees graze seagrass meadows. Cut Seagrass sharply and watch the turtles, manatees and the tiger sharks that hunt turtles.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Powers the algae, seagrass and mangroves of the shallow, sunlit waters and tidal flats around the islands.
Big tides flood and drain the mangroves and mudflats twice a day, carrying nutrients in and moving food around for crabs, fish and wading birds.
Bacteria and fungi break down mangrove leaves, dead algae and carcasses, returning nutrients to the mud.
Tidal forest that makes up large areas of the islands. A Wikipedia page on a park there says mangroves help molluscs, fish and sea turtles breed.

nodes.name: Microalgae and phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny algae in the water and on mudflats. They feed zooplankton, crabs and grazing fish.

nodes.name: Coastal grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses on shores and clearings that hippos graze after leaving the water at night.
Common on the islands. Its fruit is a main food for palm-nut vultures.
Tiny drifting grazers of phytoplankton that feed on algae and in turn feed small fish.

nodes.name: Fiddler crab
nodes.desc: Burrowing crab of muddy shores that sifts algae and detritus from sediment. Wading birds feed on crabs like it.
Coastal fish that grazes algae and detritus on mud and sand, a staple prey of inshore dolphins.
Adults graze mainly seagrasses and algae. Tiger sharks are their main predator.
Eats plants growing on or over the water. In estuaries it feeds on mangrove foliage. Guinea-Bissau is among the countries with most manatees.
Rests in water and comes ashore at night to graze grass. Its carcasses feed vultures.
Migrant wader that winters on African coasts, probing mud for worms, small shellfish and crustaceans.
Lives in shallow coastal and estuarine water and mainly eats inshore schooling fish such as mullet.
Fish-eating raptor that dives for fish in coastal waters; recorded often in the area.
Eats mostly oil-palm fruit, plus crabs, fish and carrion. Common in coastal forests and mangrove swamps.
Small scavenging vulture; GloBI records it feeding on hippo carcasses.
Main predator of adult green turtles, often hunting near nesting beaches.
